title: Prayer
lead: Speaking to God: praise, thanks, confession, lament and asking, alone or for the people. The Bible's prayers range from Abraham's bargaining for Sodom to the Lord's Prayer, and Solomon's prayer at the Temple made Jerusalem the place toward which Jews still pray.

sections.b: Prayer in the Bible is speech to God in every mood. Abraham pleads for Sodom (Genesis 18:22–33), Moses stands in the gap for Israel (Exodus 32:11–14), Hannah pours out her heart at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1:10–16), and Solomon dedicates the temple with a prayer that God will hear from heaven whatever is prayed toward it (1 Kings 8:22–53). Elijah prays for fire and for rain (1 Kings 18:36–37, 18:42), Hezekiah spreads a threatening letter before the LORD (2 Kings 19:14–19), and Daniel prays toward Jerusalem three times a day (Daniel 6:10). The Psalms are Israel's prayer book of praise and lament. Jesus prays alone and teaches his followers the Lord's Prayer (Matthew 6:9–13; Luke 11:1–4), calls the temple "a house of prayer" (Mark 11:17), and prays in Gethsemane. Paul urges believers to pray without ceasing (1 Thessalonians 5:17).
